# Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)ABSD is a stamp duty payable on top of Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) when purchasing residential property in Singapore. It applies to Singapore Citizens buying a second or subsequent property, all Permanent Residents, all Foreigners, and all entities.## Current ABSD Rates (effective 27 April 2023)### Singapore Citizens (SC)
- 1st residential property: 0%
- 2nd residential property: 20%
- 3rd and subsequent residential property: 30%### Singapore Permanent Residents (PR)
- 1st residential property: 5%
- 2nd residential property: 30%
- 3rd and subsequent residential property: 35%### Foreigners (non-SC, non-PR)
- Any residential property: 60%### Entities (companies, trusts)
- Any residential property: 65%
- Housing developers: 35% (remittable on application subject to conditions)## Key Rules

ABSD must be paid in full within 14 days of the date of the Option to Purchase (OTP) or Sale and Purchase Agreement (S&P). It cannot be paid from a bank loan. It must come from cash or CPF Ordinary Account funds.### Counting Properties
The number of residential properties owned is counted at the time of purchase, including properties held jointly. Partial interests count as ownership.### Joint Purchases (Mixed Citizenship)
For joint purchases between a SC and a foreigner, the higher ABSD rate (foreigner rate) applies to the entire purchase price.
For joint purchases between a SC and a PR, the PR rate applies.### Married Couples — SC Couples Buying First Home Together
A SC married to a SC buying their first residential property together: 0% ABSD, provided neither has previously owned residential property.
A SC married to a PR buying their first home: PR rate (5%) applies on the entire transaction.

A SC couple may apply for ABSD remission when selling one existing property and buying a replacement property, if both own only one property and the first property is sold within 6 months of purchasing the replacement.## ABSD and HDB Flats
HDB flats are residential properties for ABSD counting purposes.
A SC who owns one HDB flat buying a private condo pays 20% ABSD (2nd property rate).
A PR who owns one HDB flat buying any property pays 30% ABSD (2nd property rate).## ABSD Payment Mechanics
- Due: within 14 days of OTP exercise or S&P signing (whichever is earlier)
- Payable to: IRAS
- Payment methods: cash or CPF OA (CPF portion subject to CPF withdrawal limits)
- Late payment: 6% penalty per annum on unpaid ABSD

ABSD was first introduced in December 2011. Rates have been revised multiple times:
- Dec 2011: first introduction
- Jan 2013: rates increased
- Jul 2018: significant increase (foreigners moved from 15% to 20%)
- Dec 2021: further increases
- Apr 2023: current rates (foreigners: 60%, entities: 65%)Always verify effective_date before transacting. Policy rates are subject to government review.

# Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD)BSD is a stamp duty payable by the buyer on all property purchases in Singapore. It applies to all buyers regardless of citizenship, residency, or number of properties owned. # CPF Usage Rules for Property PurchaseCPF Ordinary Account (OA) funds can be used to purchase residential property in Singapore. Usage is subject to several limits and eligibility conditions.## CPF Accounts Overview- **Ordinary Account (OA)**: 2.5% per annum interest. Usable for property, investment, education.
- **Special Account (SA)**: 4.0% per annum interest. Locked for retirement — cannot be used for property.
- **MediSave**: Locked for healthcare — cannot be used for property.All property-related CPF usage comes from the OA only.## Properties Where CPF OA Can Be Used### HDB Flats
- Fully eligible for HDB concessionary loan repayments
- Eligible for bank loan down payment and monthly instalments
- Subject to Valuation Limit (VL) and remaining lease conditions### Private Residential Properties (Condos, Landed)
- Eligible for down payment and monthly mortgage instalments
- Subject to Valuation Limit and Withdrawal Limit
- Subject to remaining lease conditions### Properties NOT Eligible for CPF Usage
- Commercial properties
- Industrial properties
- Properties with remaining lease below 20 years## Key CPF Usage Limits

Total CPF withdrawn for a property (by all owners) cannot exceed the lower of:
- Purchase price of the property
- Valuation at time of purchaseOnce VL is reached, no more CPF OA can be withdrawn for that property.### Withdrawal Limit (WL)
Total CPF withdrawn can exceed VL up to 120% of VL, but only if:
- The property's remaining lease covers the youngest owner to at least age 95If remaining lease does NOT cover youngest owner to age 95:
- CPF usage is capped at the VL (no excess above VL)
- Further, if remaining lease is less than 30 years, CPF usage is prorated based on the ratio of (remaining lease / (95 - youngest owner's age))## Remaining Lease and CPF — Detailed Rules### Remaining Lease >= 30 Years AND Covers Youngest Owner to Age 95
- Full CPF usage up to Valuation Limit
- Withdrawal Limit (120% of VL) also available

AND Covers Youngest Owner to Age 95
- Full CPF usage up to Valuation Limit
- Withdrawal Limit (120% of VL) also available### Remaining Lease >= 20 Years but Does NOT Cover Youngest Owner to Age 95
- CPF usage capped at prorated VL
- Prorated VL = VL × (remaining lease) / (95 - youngest owner's age)
- No access to Withdrawal Limit### Remaining Lease < 20 Years
- CPF CANNOT be used at all for this property## CPF Usage and Buyer Age — ExampleScenario: SC buyer, age 45, buying HDB flat with 55 years remaining lease
- Coverage check: 55 years remaining → buyer would be 45 + 55 = 100 at end of lease → covers to age 95 ✓
- Full CPF usage up to VL and WL

- Coverage check: 40 years → buyer would be 50 + 40 = 90 at end of lease → does NOT cover to age 95
- CPF usage prorated: VL × 40 / (95 - 50) = VL × 40/45 = 88.9% of VLScenario: SC buyer, age 55, buying HDB flat with 15 years remaining lease
- Remaining lease < 20 years → NO CPF usage at all## CPF OA as Opportunity CostMoney in CPF OA earns a guaranteed 2.5% per annum (first SGD 20,000 earns 3.5% — Medisave top-up floor). Using CPF OA for property means:
- Forgoing the 2.5% guaranteed return
- Property must appreciate or yield rentally above 2.5% to justify CPF usage

- All CPF principal withdrawn must be refunded to OA
- Accrued interest at 2.5% per annum on the withdrawn amount must also be refunded
- Only the proceeds above (principal + accrued interest) represent cash profit
- This can significantly reduce apparent cash profit on sale## CPF for ABSD and BSDCPF OA can also be used to pay:

- No minimum cash down payment required (entire 20% down payment can be from CPF OA)
- Monthly instalments can be fully serviced from CPF OA

# Loan-to-Value (LTV) LimitThe LTV limit caps the maximum loan a financial institution may grant relative to the property's value (or purchase price, whichever is lower). It determines the minimum down payment required.## Current LTV Limits for Bank Loans (Private Property and HDB)### First Housing Loan
- LTV limit: 75%
- Minimum down payment: 25%
  - At least 5% must be paid in cash
  - The remaining 20% may be from CPF OA or cash### Second Housing Loan (Outstanding Loan Exists)
- LTV limit: 45%
- Minimum down payment: 55%
  - At least 25% must be paid in cash
  - Remaining 30% may be from CPF OA or cash### Third and Subsequent Housing Loans
- LTV limit: 35%
- Minimum down payment: 65%
  - At least 25% must be paid in cash## Age and Tenure Conditions

TV limit: 35%
- Minimum down payment: 65%
  - At least 25% must be paid in cash## Age and Tenure ConditionsIf the loan tenure extends beyond the borrower's age of 65, or if the tenure exceeds 30 years, the LTV is reduced:
- First loan: reduced from 75% to 55% (minimum cash down payment: 10%)
- Second loan: reduced from 45% to 25%Loan tenure is capped at 30 years for HDB loans (25 years for HDB concessionary loans) and 35 years for bank loans on private property.## HDB Concessionary Loan LTVHDB's own concessionary loan (2.6% interest) offers:
- LTV: up to 80% of purchase price or value, whichever is lower
- Minimum down payment: 20% (can be entirely from CPF OA — no mandatory cash component)
- Eligibility: Singapore Citizens only, income ceiling applies, no outstanding private property## Counting Loans

The outstanding loan count includes:
- HDB flat loans
- Private property bank loans
- Mortgages on overseas properties## Cash vs CPF for Down Payment### First Property (LTV 75%)
- Mandatory cash: 5% of purchase price
- Optional CPF: up to 20% of purchase price
- Example (SGD 1,000,000 property): SGD 50,000 cash + SGD 200,000 CPF + SGD 750,000 loan

Example (SGD 1,000,000 property): SGD 50,000 cash + SGD 200,000 CPF + SGD 750,000 loan### Second Property (LTV 45%)
- Mandatory cash: 25% of purchase price
- Optional CPF: up to 30% of purchase price
- ABSD (SC 2nd property: 20%) must also be paid in cash/CPF, not from loan
- Example (SGD 1,500,000 condo): SGD 375,000 cash + SGD 450,000 CPF + SGD 675,000 loan + SGD 300,000 ABSD## Valuation and LTVLTV is applied on the lower of:
- Purchase price agreed in OTP/S&P
- Bank's independent valuation of the propertyIf valuation is below purchase price (known as "cash over valuation" or COV):
- The difference must be paid fully in cash
- LTV loan is computed on the lower valuation, not the purchase price## LTV for ForeignersLTV limits apply equally to foreigners, PRs, and citizens. The same first/second/third loan tiers apply. However, foreigners face 60% ABSD on top of the down payment requirement.

, and citizens. The same first/second/third loan tiers apply. However, foreigners face 60% ABSD on top of the down payment requirement.## Historical Changes
- Sep 2022: second loan LTV tightened from 45% to 45% (no change to LTV, but ABSD raised)

# Mortgage Servicing Ratio (MSR)MSR limits the portion of a borrower's gross monthly income that can be used for mortgage repayments on HDB flats and Executive Condominiums (ECs). It applies on top of TDSR.## Current MSR Threshold: 30%Monthly mortgage repayments for the HDB flat or EC being purchased must not exceed 30% of the borrower's gross monthly income.## Properties MSR Applies ToMSR applies when buying:
1. HDB flats (new BTO, resale, DBSS) — financed by HDB loan or bank loan
2. Executive Condominiums (ECs) — only for bank loans (not HDB loans, since ECs are private)MSR does NOT apply to private condominiums or landed properties.## MSR vs TDSRFor HDB and EC purchases, BOTH MSR and TDSR must be satisfied:
- MSR: monthly HDB/EC mortgage repayment ≤ 30% of gross monthly income
- TDSR: total monthly debt repayments ≤ 55% of gross monthly incomeMSR is typically the binding constraint because 30% < 55%.## MSR Calculation Example

total monthly debt repayments ≤ 55% of gross monthly incomeMSR is typically the binding constraint because 30% < 55%.## MSR Calculation ExampleGross monthly income: SGD 8,000
MSR limit: 30% × 8,000 = SGD 2,400/month maximum mortgage repaymentAt a 3.5% interest rate over 25 years:
Maximum loan ≈ SGD 2,400 × 151 (annuity factor) ≈ SGD 430,000## Income Definition for MSRSame rules as TDSR:
- Fixed salary: 100% of gross monthly salary
- Variable/commission income: 70% of 12-month average
- Rental income: 70% of gross rental
- Self-employment: 70% of 2-year average NOA## MSR and Joint BorrowersFor joint applications, the combined gross monthly income of all borrowers is used, subject to lender assessment.## HDB Loan vs Bank Loan — MSR Interaction

BorrowersFor joint applications, the combined gross monthly income of all borrowers is used, subject to lender assessment.## HDB Loan vs Bank Loan — MSR Interaction### HDB Concessionary Loan
- Interest rate: 0.1% above CPF OA rate (currently ~2.6%)
- MSR applies: monthly repayment must not exceed 30% of gross monthly income
- HDB uses the actual loan interest rate for MSR assessment (no stress-test rate)### Bank Loan for HDB Flat
- MSR applies at 30%
- Bank uses stress-test rate of 4.0% for MSR/TDSR assessment
- LTV limit is 75% (lower than HDB loan's 80%)## Practical Impact of MSRMSR significantly constrains the loan quantum for HDB flat buyers, particularly in high-price towns like Bishan, Queenstown, or Toa Payoh.

- 25% down payment: SGD 275,000

- Monthly repayment at 3.5% over 25 years: ~SGD 4,100

MSR was introduced in August 2013 at 30% for HDB flat purchases, extended to ECs in December 2013. The 30% threshold has remained unchanged since introduction.

# Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)TDSR limits the proportion of a borrower's gross monthly income that can go towards servicing all debt obligations. It applies to all property loans granted by financial institutions in Singapore.## Current TDSR Threshold: 55%A borrower's total monthly debt repayments — including the new property loan being applied for — must not exceed 55% of their gross monthly income.## What Counts as DebtAll outstanding loan obligations are included in the TDSR calculation:
- Property loans (existing and the new loan being applied for)
- Car loans
- Personal loans and credit lines
- Student loans
- Credit card outstanding balances (counted at 5% of the outstanding balance as a monthly obligation)
- Any other credit facilities## Income Definition for TDSR### Employment Income
- Fixed salary: 100% of gross monthly salary
- Variable income (bonuses, commission): 70% of the average over 12 months### Rental Income
- 70% of gross rental income (after deducting property tax and maintenance)### Self-Employment / Business Income
- 70% of average monthly income (assessed over 2 years of NOA)

tax and maintenance)### Self-Employment / Business Income
- 70% of average monthly income (assessed over 2 years of NOA)### Investment Income
- Dividends, interest: assessed case by case by lender## TDSR Calculation ExampleGross monthly salary: SGD 10,000
Existing car loan repayment: SGD 1,000/month
Proposed property loan repayment: SGD 3,500/month
Total debt: SGD 4,500/month
TDSR: 4,500 / 10,000 = 45% → passes TDSR (below 55%)If property loan were SGD 5,000/month:
TDSR: 6,000 / 10,000 = 60% → fails TDSR (above 55%)## Stress-Test Rate for TDSRFinancial institutions must apply a minimum stress-test interest rate of 4.0% per annum when computing the monthly repayment for TDSR assessment, even if the actual loan rate is lower. This ensures borrowers can withstand rate increases.## TDSR and Investment PropertiesFor investment properties (properties not for owner-occupation), lenders may apply stricter income haircuts at their discretion.

MSR is the binding constraint for HDB purchases since 30% < 55%.## Historical Context

- Sep 2022: reduced to 55% (tightened to cool the market)
- Jul 2023: current framework confirmedAlways verify effective_date. MAS reviews TDSR periodically.
